clarification.question: What should Python vs. TypeScript optimize for?

goals.label: Best AI tooling
goals.hint: Richest libraries, models, and research support

goals.label: Ship to web apps
goals.hint: Smooth integration with frontends and full-stack code

goals.label: Reliable at scale
goals.hint: Type safety, maintainability, and deployment ease

options.name: Python
options.tagline: The default language of AI research and tooling
pros: Most ML/AI libraries and first-party SDKs
Fastest access to new research and models
cons: Harder to share code with web frontends

options.name: TypeScript
options.tagline: Strong choice for agents embedded in web products
pros: Excellent type safety for agent tool schemas
Natural fit for full-stack and edge deployments
Official SDKs from major model providers
cons: Less community material on advanced agent patterns

criteria.label: Library breadth
criteria.rationale: Python has the most AI and ML libraries available

criteria.label: Model SDK support
criteria.rationale: Both have official provider SDKs; Python gets new features first

criteria.label: Typing & tool schemas
criteria.rationale: TypeScript's static types make tool definitions safer

criteria.label: Web integration
criteria.rationale: TypeScript shares code with frontends and edge runtimes

criteria.label: Research & examples
criteria.rationale: Most papers, notebooks, and agent frameworks start in Python

verdict.summary: For the broadest AI tooling and fastest access to new research, choose Python. Pick TypeScript only if the agent is tightly coupled to a web or edge product.

options.name: Python
pros: Most agent frameworks and SDKs ship Python first
cons: Needs an API layer to reach the browser

options.name: TypeScript
options.tagline: One language across frontend and backend
pros: Shares types and code with React/Next.js frontends
Strong type safety for complex agent state
Good streaming support for chat UIs

criteria.label: Frontend fit
criteria.rationale: TypeScript shares code and types with web frontends directly

criteria.label: AI libraries
criteria.rationale: Python has more agent frameworks and ML tools

criteria.label: Type safety
criteria.rationale: TypeScript's static types help manage complex agent state

criteria.label: Streaming UX
criteria.rationale: TypeScript has strong SSE and streaming patterns for chat UIs

verdict.summary: For shipping agents into web apps, TypeScript wins on frontend integration, typing, and streaming. Choose Python only if you rely on Python-first AI libraries or research tooling.

options.name: Python
options.tagline: Dominant AI ecosystem with mature agent frameworks
pros: Deepest ML and LLM SDK support
Most agent frameworks launch here first
cons: Packaging and version management can be messy

options.name: TypeScript
options.tagline: Type-safe agents that share code with your web stack
pros: Compile-time type checks catch tool-schema errors
Shares types and code with frontend and APIs
Solid runtime for I/O-heavy agent workloads
cons: Some provider SDKs lag behind Python

criteria.label: Type safety
criteria.rationale: TypeScript's static types catch agent tool and schema bugs early.

criteria.label: Ecosystem
criteria.rationale: Python has more mature AI libraries, tooling, and examples.

criteria.label: Maintainability
criteria.rationale: Typed codebases are easier to refactor safely as agents grow.

criteria.label: Deployment
criteria.rationale: Node services and serverless fit well with typical web infrastructure.

verdict.summary: For reliability at scale, TypeScript's static typing and maintainability give it the edge, especially if your agents sit inside a web stack. Choose Python instead if you depend on niche ML libraries or need the newest agent frameworks first.
